member.name: T:DotNetCore.HayateOP.Extensions.Configuration.HayateDefaultPolicyHolder`1
member.summary: Records the object policy the configuration-driven registrations seeded when the caller supplied none, so BuildConfiguredPool<T> can tell that fallback apart from a policy the caller registered and leave the pool to derive its own policy instead of pinning this one.
member.remarks:
The mirror of the marker the DependencyInjection package keeps. Each package owns the registration and the pool build it pairs with, so each keeps its own; neither is part of a public surface.
The fallback is recognised by identity, not by type. A caller may register itself; that is the caller's policy, and it is pinned like any other, even though it is an instance of the type the library would have seeded itself.
Nothing is recorded until the container resolves the seeded registration, so a container where the caller's own policy won leaves this holder empty, and answers for that policy — which is the answer that pins it.

member.summary: Registers a HayateOP pool driven by configuration.
member.param: The configuration root used to read pool options.
Optional logical pool name; defaults to the type name of .
member.remarks: The pool's object policy is the library default, or a policy registered directly in the container, which this overload honours rather than replaces. The default policy takes its reset timing from the merged configuration's ResetOnReturn / ResetOnBorrow values, so setting them in appsettings reaches the pool; a policy registered directly in the container is pinned instead and keeps whatever reset its own OnRelease / OnAcquire implement.
member.exception: Thrown when the merged pool configuration is invalid.

member.name: M:Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ConfigurationExtensions.RegisterNamedHayatePool``1(DotNetCore.HayateOP.IHayateServiceCollection,Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.IConfiguration,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Registers a named pool of type driven by configuration: the configuration-driven counterpart of AddNamedPool<T>(name).
member.param: The configuration root used to read pool options.
The logical pool name; also the name of the per-pool configuration section ({configSectionPath}:Pools:{name}).
member.exception: Thrown when the merged pool configuration is invalid.
member.remarks: The pool is registered under the canonical name {typeof(T).Name}:{name} and resolved through , so a configuration-driven named pool coexists with the unnamed pool of the same type and with any other name — exactly as a pool declared with AddNamedPool does. Section merging and hot reload behave as they do for : the global section is applied first and only the keys present in the pool's own section override it. Its object policy is the library default, or a policy registered directly in the container; when it is the default, this name's ResetOnReturn / ResetOnBorrow values reach it, so two names of one element type can run different timings.

member.name: M:Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ConfigurationExtensions.SeedDefaultPolicy``1(Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.IServiceCollection,System.Func{System.IServiceProvider,DotNetCore.HayateOP.Policies.IHayateObjectPolicy{``0}})
member.summary: Seeds with — the library default — but only when the container has no policy for the element type yet, and marks the instance so can leave a pool built with it to derive its own policy.
member.remarks:
The seeding keeps the effect the TryAddSingleton it replaces had: when a descriptor already exists — the caller registered a policy, in either order relative to this call — nothing is added and nothing is replaced.
What it adds is the record of the instance it seeded. A pool whose policy turns out to be that fallback is built without WithPolicy, so the builder derives the policy from the pool's own options — the only route the ResetOnReturn / ResetOnBorrow switches have into a policy, and the route an appsettings file sets those switches through. A policy the caller registered is pinned as before, and its own reset is never moved by the switches.
The policy is created on first request rather than here, so a type the default policy cannot construct still reports that when its pool is built, not when it is declared.
member.param: The service collection the pool is being registered in.
